EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  June 26, 2017

CALL TO ORDER
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ called the meeting to order, the time being 7:00 p.m. in the Rolling
Hills Estates City Council Chambers.

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT
Chairman Velveth Schmitz
Susan Brtis
Patricia Harik
Bill Kemp
Lou Persichina
Vicki Shinn
Carrie Silvano

STAFF MEMBER PRESENT
Andy Clark, Community Services Director

DRAFT MINUTES OF MAY 30, 2017
MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER PERSICHINA

  TO APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE MAY 30, 2017 SPECIAL
  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

THERE BEING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, inquired about the upcoming footing improvement
project planned for the Chandler Park arena. She noted that she and some Trainers are
concerned about the northeast corner of the arena being slightly higher than the rest of the
arena and that additional sand may be needed. Ms. Schachter also presented information
about a new sand stabilizer material, known as ArenaAid, which could be considered for this
footing improvement project.

Chairman Schmitz requested that an update on this project be agendized for the next
Equestrian Committee meeting.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 26, 2017  1
 PV PENINSULA WATER RELIABILITY PROJECT TEMPORARY HORSE BOARDING
LOGISTICS
Nancy Wildman, 34 Pony Lane, reported her recent communications Gil Houle, Peter Weber
Equestrian Center (PWEC) concessionaire. He believes that the logistics of using Ernie
Howlett Park’s barn and serviced by his staff would not be conducive for his operations.
Instead, Mr. Houle stated that he would use any vacant PWEC stalls to temporarily
accommodate displaced horses, and if necessary, he could construct eight 12-foot by 24-foot
pipe corrals for temporary boarding needs.

Ms. Wildman indicated that from her recent tours of the bridle trails that she noticed that there
were a number of vacant stalls and barns, which may also be temporarily available after
contacting each owner. She estimated that there may be a need to relocate up to 20 horses
during this project. In response to CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ inquiry, it was reported that the
project is scheduled to occur between June and October 2018 and therefore there was ample
lead time to prepare for the temporary relocations. Ms. Wildman noted that Gil Houle had
indicated that he would need 30 days’ notice to construct the eight temporary stalls.

Angie Gilbride, Regional Community Affairs Specialist for California Water Service Company,
stated that company representatives would be meeting with all the horse owners along this
section of trail in about 30 days. In response to the Community Services Director’s inquiry,
Ms. Gilbride stated that monthly boarding fees at the temporary boarding sites would be paid
for by California Water Service Company. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ asked Ms. Gilbride to keep
the Community Services Director apprised of the meetings with horse owners.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

PORTABLE WATER STORAGE UNIT COSTS, WATER TRUCK PURCHASE AND
RENTAL INFORMATION
The Community Services Director indicated that the MEMBER DEAN-PORTER and the City’s
Maintenance Supervisor had met to compare costs of purchasing new and used water trucks
with leasing water trucks. In addition, they reviewed the prices of new and used water trailers,
which can be hitched onto a pick-up truck. CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ stated that staff had
collected valuable cost information which could be used in the future, should there be a need
to lease or purchase equipment for arena watering needs.

In addition, the Community Services Director stated that follow-up conversations with Horse
Show organizers Becky Martin, Larry Lean, and Lynda Palmer found that none of them were
having any issues with watering the arenas they used. All of them thoroughly watered the
arenas on the evening before their Horse Shows and then again during a break in the shows’
schedules prior to the afternoon winds that occur at Howlett Park. The Portuguese Bend
National Horse Show, however, needed a water truck for their multi-day show not only for
watering the arenas multiple times during each day, but to also water down the parking lot.

The Community Services Director reported that staff was researching a water sprayer which
could be attached to the City’s 500-gallon portable water tank. Pam Schachter noted Arena
#1’s center is dry and Horse Shows would benefit from a water truck watering that area.
EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 26, 2017  2
 HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN SERVICES LICENCES AND PERMITS SUBCOMMITTEE UPDATE
The Community Services Director thanked Members Silvano, Brtis, Kemp, and Dean-Porter
for participating in a follow-up meeting with the Administrative Services Department staff,
which oversee the issuance of City Business Licenses. He briefly reviewed the staff report
which outlined four conclusions that the Subcommittee had made after identifying at least 16
types of paid equestrian services occurring in the City, other than Horse Trainer and manure
removal services. It was noted that the Administrative Services Department was working with
MuniServices to not only have them assist in the collection of unpaid Business Licenses, but
to combine or eliminate some of the license categories and also consider increasing some
fees.

Discussion ensued regarding Horse Exercisers, which was being recommended by the
Subcommittee to require a City Business License. It was determined that the majority of
those service providers were not making enough income to meet the $2,500 minimum
requirement to purchase a Business License and would be difficult to enforce.

MEMBER SILVANO moved, seconded by MEMBER BRTIS

  THAT THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION TO RECOMMEND THAT CITY COUNCIL:

  1.  DIRECT THE ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DEPARTMENT STAFF AND
  MUNISERVICES TO REQUIRE THE FOLLOWING EQUESTRIAN SERVICE
  PROVIDERS TO OBTAIN CITY BUSINESS LICENSES: VETERINARIANS,
  EQUINE DENTISTS, EQUINE CHIROPRACTORS, EQUINE MASSAGE
  THERAPISTS, FARRIERS, TRAIL RIDE OPERATORS, AND HORSE
  HAULERS; AND

  2.  DIRECT THE ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DEPARTMENT STAFF TO
  WORK WITH MUNISERVICES TO CONSIDER THE DEVELOPMENT OF AN
  EQUESTRIAN SERVICES BUSINESS LICENSE CATEGORY.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ SO ORDERED.

EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG
CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ noted that there had been no significant issues reported to staff since
the May Equestrian Committee meeting.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ RECEIVED AND FILED THE REPORT.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 26, 2017  3
 COMMITTEE MEMBER REPORTS

A.  ADOPT-A-TRAIL REPORTS
  MEMBER HARIK reported that the deep erosion on the upper trail section of bridle trail
  in the George F Canyon Nature Preserve had been improved.

  Pam Schachter reported that there had been a water main line break that morning
  which had flooded the Botanical Gardens Trail resulting in water in the Crenshaw
  Tunnel. In addition, she noted that arena sprinklers had also malfunctioned that
  morning flooding the Chandler Park arena.

B.  HOWLETT PARK JUDGE’S BOOTH PROJECT UPDATE
  The Community Services Director reported that the forms were installed to pour
  concrete bases for the new Horse Show and Dressage Show Judges Booths.
  Unfortunately, due to the amount of local construction projects, it was taking some time
  to have concrete delivered. Both Judges Booths are completed and waiting for the
  concrete bases to be completed in order to deliver and install them in Howlett Park.

C.  CITY CELEBRATION HORSEMANSHIP EVENTS
  MEMBER SHINN asked for and received Committee Members’ commitments to assist
  her at the 60th Annual City Celebration horsemanship events on September 23 rd in
  Ernie Howlett Park.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS
A.  ANNUAL EQUESTRIAN IMPROVEMENTS AND ACTIVITIES REPORT

B.  CHANDLER PARK ARENA FOOTING PROJECT UPDATE

C.  EQUINE EMERGENCY WATER SOURCES STRATEGY

ADJOURNMENT
MEMBER PERSICHINA moved, seconded by MEMBER SHINN

  TO ADJOURN THE EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING.

HEARING NO OBJECTION, CHAIRMAN SCHMITZ ADJOURNED THE MEETING.

The meeting adjourned at 7:43 p.m.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES
JUNE 26, 2017  4
 Respectfully submitted,

Andy Clark
Community Services Director
